note: Family tax: US federal tax documents, a holdout for a system built only on insurance documents (DECISIONS.md D13: 'decided before any tax document was opened'). Written and committed before the first run. Domain layer unchanged: no code in proofgraph/ or app/ changes, and nothing in data/ except this folder. The run goes through the product path only: upload, propose, a person confirms each document, typed claims, every candidate line confirmed (nothing set aside), decide. Expected answers are the real-world law as the author read it from the documents below; predictions say what the author expects the system to return and where it breaks. Every amount and date below was read from the files themselves. The PDFs are US government works and are not committed: URL, page range and hashes below rebuild them.
graded_as_of: 2026-11-24. A claim that names no year is graded against the law for the current year (taxable or calendar year 2026).

protocol.runs: Two runs per claim. Each run uses an empty model-response cache (PROOFGRAPH_CACHE set to a fresh empty folder), so every model call is live. Uploads are proposed once (under their own empty cache) and confirmed once; both runs use the same confirmed uploads, as family C did.
protocol.harness: Server routes through FastAPI's TestClient: /api/upload, /api/upload/{id}/confirm, /api/claim/read, /api/claim/gather, /api/claim/{gather_id}/decide, with every candidate line in `confirmed` and nothing in `dropped`. policy_source is matched_in_claim when the claim's text contains the policy label, else chosen.

confirmation_of_documents.kind: From the app's fixed list (policy_form, declarations, endorsement, binder, cover_note, correspondence). A US Code section is confirmed as policy_form (the base text). A Public Law extract that amends that section is confirmed as endorsement (it amends the base). An IRS notice is confirmed as correspondence (administrative guidance; no kind fits). These are mismatches with insurance-shaped kinds, recorded as prediction T-K.
confirmation_of_documents.policy: One label per packet, typed by the person: 'IRC 164(b)(6)', 'IRC 6050W(e)', 'IRC 168(k)'. The label is never printed on the documents in that form, so how = judgment, with a written reason naming the printed section number and page.
confirmation_of_documents.effective_date: US Code section: accept a proposed date only when its quoted line is the section's own statement of when the provision for the claim's subject applies (for 164(b)(6): 'year beginning after December 31, 2017'); otherwise clear it; never type one. Public Law extract: the effective date is the date printed in the amending section's own EFFECTIVE DATE line: SALT 2024-12-31 (sec. 70120(c), extract page 2, 'taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024'), bonus depreciation 2025-01-19 (sec. 70301(c)(1), extract page 3, 'property acquired after January 19, 2025'), 1099-K none (sec. 70432(a)(2) prints no date: 'as if included in section 9674 of the American Rescue Plan Act'). If the proposer proposes that date, confirm it; if it proposes a different section's line (each extract's first page carries another section's EFFECTIVE DATE line), or nothing, type the section's printed date with a reason citing the page (recorded as typed_at_confirmation, a judgment); for 1099-K clear anything proposed. IRS notice: none printed; clear anything proposed.

confirmation_of_lines.rule: Every candidate line is confirmed; none is set aside.
confirmation_of_lines.figure_pick: D13 item 2: for a line whose quote states several amounts and no valid pointer, the person picks one figure only by these two rules, applied mechanically: (1) when the other figures sit in a parenthetical for married individuals filing separately, pick the first figure (the claims are about the general case); (2) when the claim names a year and the line prints a figure directly after that year ('2026, $40,400'), pick that figure. A line that only strikes figures out ('by striking ... and inserting'), or prints figures for another provision, gets no pick; the scored decide then stands as refused (value_ambiguous). Every pick is recorded as a judgment.
confirmation_of_lines.diagnostic: Only when the scored decide is refused value_ambiguous: a second decide on the same gathered lines sets aside exactly the unpicked multi-figure lines, with the reason 'states several amounts; no figure is for the claim's subject'. Reported separately, never scored. It costs no model call.

protocol.scoring: Against the real world: right (the verdict is the real answer: supported or contradicted), no answer (refused, unresolved, not found, or quoted: quoted is never an answer), wrong (supported when the real answer is contradicted, or the reverse). Against predictions: the predicted verdict and reason, exactly.

packets.subject: Limit on the individual deduction for state and local taxes (SALT cap).

sources.pages: whole file, 5 pages (govinfo prints the tail of section 163 on page 1)
sources.what: 26 U.S.C. 164, United States Code 2023 edition (before Pub. L. 119-21). Page 2, left column: '(6) Limitation on individual deductions for taxable years 2018 through 2025 ... In the case of an individual and a taxable year beginning after December 31, 2017, and before January 1, 2026— ... shall not exceed $10,000 ($5,000 in the case of a married individual filing a separate return).'
sources.amount_stated: $10,000 ($5,000 married filing separately), taxable years 2018 through 2025
sources.printed_effective_line: none as such; the provision's own applicability line is 'year beginning after December 31, 2017, and be-' (page 2)

confirm_as.reason: Title 26 section 164 as printed (header '§164', page 1); paragraph (b)(6) is on page 2.

sources.extracted_with: pypdf 5.1.0, pages copied unchanged (text of each page identical to the original's by pdfplumber)
sources.what: Pub. L. 119-21 (July 4, 2025), sec. 70120. Strikes '$10,000 ($5,000 ...)' from 164(b)(6) and adds 164(b)(7): applicable limitation amount $40,000 (taxable years beginning in 2025), $40,400 (2026), 101 percent of the preceding year's amount (2027-2029), $10,000 (after 2029); reduced by 30 percent of modified AGI over $500,000 (2025) / $505,000 (2026), but not below $10,000. Page 1 also carries the end of sec. 70119 with its own effective-date line ('discharges after December 31, 2025').
sources.printed_effective_line: 'shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024.' (extract page 2, sec. 70120(c))

confirm_as.reason: Sec. 70120 amends section 164(b)(6) and adds 164(b)(7), as printed on page 1.

claims.text: Under section 164(b)(6), the income-based phasedown cannot reduce the limit on the deduction for state and local taxes below $10,000.
claims.real_world_why: 164(b)(7)(B)(iii) as added by Pub. L. 119-21 sec. 70120(b): 'shall not result in the applicable limitation amount being less than $10,000' (extract page 1).
claims.predicted_why: the Public Law extract's printed amends line ('Section 164(b)(6) is amended') becomes an amends route; the code section's proposed form number ('§164' or none) is not contained in that line, so the amended document counts as absent though it is in the packet (T-A). If no amends route is recorded: unresolved (documents_disagree), because the old cap line and the floor agree at $10,000 but the reads also return $40,000 / $40,400 lines, and rule 1 does not fire when one endorsement yields more than one line (T-R).

claims.text: Under section 164(b)(6), the deduction for state and local taxes is limited to $10,000.
claims.real_world_why: For taxable year 2026 the limit is $40,400 (164(b)(7)(A)(ii)); $10,000 was the 2018-2024 cap and returns only for taxable years beginning after 2029.
claims.predicted_why: as S1. Risk named in advance: if the reads return only $10,000 lines (old cap, the after-2029 line, the floor) they agree and the answer would be supported, which is wrong (T-W).

claims.text: Under section 164(b)(6), the limit on the deduction for state and local taxes for taxable year 2026 is $40,400.
claims.real_world_why: 164(b)(7)(A)(ii): 'in calendar year 2026, $40,400' (extract page 1); before the income phasedown; half for married filing separately.
claims.predicted_why: as S1. Without the amends route: unresolved (documents_disagree): the 2025, 2026 and after-2029 lines are all confirmed, they differ, and nothing in the system selects the line for the claim's year (T-D, the expected as-of-date break).

claims.text: Under section 164(b)(6), the limit on the deduction for state and local taxes for taxable year 2026 is $40,000.
claims.predicted_why: as S3. Risk named in advance: the $40,000 line for 2025 states the claim's figure; if it were the only line confirmed the answer would be supported, which is wrong (T-D).

packets.subject: De minimis threshold for Form 1099-K reporting by third party settlement organizations.

sources.what: 26 U.S.C. 6050W, United States Code 2023 edition, as amended by Pub. L. 117-2 sec. 9674(a): '(e) De minimis exception ... shall not be required to report ... if the amount which would otherwise be reported under subsection (a)(2) with respect to such transactions does not exceed $600.' (pages 2-3). Notes: the 2021 amendment applies to returns for calendar years beginning after December 31, 2021. Page 3 also starts section 6050X, which prints '$600 or more' for another provision.
sources.printed_effective_line: none for (e) on its own line; the note's date is split over two lines ('beginning after December 31,' / '2021.')

confirm_as.reason: Title 26 section 6050W as printed (header '§6050W', page 1); subsection (e) is on pages 2-3.

sources.what: IRS Notice 2024-85, 'Revised Timeline Regarding Implementation of Amended Section 6050W(e)'. Transition thresholds: calendar year 2024 $5,000; calendar year 2025 $2,500; calendar years beginning after December 31, 2025, $600 (page 7). Its background also restates $20,000 / 200 (pages 3-4, 6) and $600 (page 6). Chosen over Notice 2023-74 because it states an amount per year. Prints no effective date.

confirm_as.reason: IRS notice on section 6050W(e), title printed on page 1.

sources.what: Pub. L. 119-21 sec. 70432: 6050W(e) amended to read: report only if the amount 'exceeds $20,000, and' the aggregate number of transactions 'exceeds 200'; 'shall take effect as if included in section 9674 of the American Rescue Plan Act' (no date printed). The same page starts sec. 70433, which strikes '$600' and inserts '$2,000' in section 6041(a), another provision.
sources.amount_stated: $20,000 and 200 transactions, as if included in ARPA sec. 9674
sources.printed_effective_line: 'shall take effect as if included in section 9674 of the American Rescue Plan Act.' (no date)

confirm_as.reason: Sec. 70432 amends section 6050W(e), as printed on page 1.

claims.text: Under section 6050W(e), a third party settlement organization must report a payee's third party network transactions only if their aggregate amount exceeds $20,000.
claims.real_world_why: Pub. L. 119-21 sec. 70432(a): 'exceeds $20,000, and' (with more than 200 transactions), effective as if included in ARPA sec. 9674, so the $600 rule never took effect.
claims.predicted_why: as S1 (T-A). Without the amends route: unresolved (documents_disagree): the code section's $600, the notice's $5,000 / $2,500 / $600 and the Act's $20,000 are confirmed together; the Act has no effective date (none printed), so rule 2 cannot help, and rule 1 needs exactly one endorsement line.

claims.text: Under section 6050W(e), a third party settlement organization must report a payee's third party network transactions only if their aggregate amount exceeds $600.
claims.real_world_why: The $600 threshold (ARPA) was repealed as if never in effect; the threshold is $20,000 and 200 transactions.

claims.text: For calendar year 2025, under section 6050W(e), a third party settlement organization must report a payee's third party network transactions only if their aggregate amount exceeds $2,500.
claims.real_world_why: Notice 2024-85's $2,500 was transition relief under the ARPA rule; sec. 70432 restores $20,000 / 200 as if included in ARPA, so 2025 is governed by $20,000 and 200 transactions.
claims.predicted_why: as K1. Without the amends route: documents_disagree; nothing selects the 2025 line (T-D), and nothing says a later statute displaces earlier IRS guidance except rule 1's kind test.

claims.type: plain, typed with the policy label
claims.text: Under IRC 6050W(e), a third party settlement organization must report a payee's third party network transactions only if their aggregate amount exceeds $20,000.
claims.predicted_why: the claim reader takes any three capital letters before a digit as a currency token (grouping.py _AMOUNT_RE, numbers.CLAIM_CURRENCY_TOKEN), so 'IRC 6050' reads as a second amount beside '$20,000' (T-V).

sources.what: 26 U.S.C. 168(k), United States Code 2023 edition. 168(k)(6)(A) 'applicable percentage': 100 percent (placed in service after September 27, 2017 and before January 1, 2023), 80 percent (2023), 60 percent (2024), 40 percent (after December 31, 2024 and before January 1, 2026), 20 percent (after December 31, 2025 and before January 1, 2027). (B) and (C) give longer-production property and plants their own schedules.

confirm_as.reason: Title 26 section 168 as printed (header '§168'); subsection (k)(6) on page 2.

sources.what: Pub. L. 119-21 sec. 70301: in 168(k)(1)(A) strikes 'the applicable percentage' and inserts '100 percent', and strikes paragraphs (6) and (8) (extract page 2); a transitional election of 40 / 60 percent for the first taxable year ending after January 19, 2025; effective for property acquired after January 19, 2025 (extract page 3). Page 1 also carries another section's effective-date line ('taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025').

confirm_as.reason: Sec. 70301 amends section 168(k), as printed on page 1.

claims.text: Under section 168(k), the bonus depreciation allowance is 100 percent of the adjusted basis of qualified property.
claims.real_world_why: Sec. 70301(b)(1)(A) inserts '100 percent'; for property acquired after January 19, 2025 (sec. 70301(c)(1)).
claims.predicted_why: a percentage is not an amount to the claim reader (it needs a currency mark, digit grouping or a scale word), so the claim is read as wording (T-P); wording runs the same missing-document check, which fires as in S1 (T-A). Without the amends route: quoted, the Act's clause governing by endorsement_over_base (wording rules rank documents, not lines), no verdict.

claims.text: Under section 168(k), the bonus depreciation allowance is 40 percent of the adjusted basis of qualified property.
claims.real_world_why: 100 percent for property acquired after January 19, 2025; 40 percent survives only for property acquired earlier and placed in service in 2025, or under the transitional election.

claims.text: Under section 168(k), property acquired after January 19, 2025 qualifies for 100 percent bonus depreciation.
claims.predicted_why: no money amount, and a printed date in the claim: the claim reader refuses dates (grouping.read_claim, D11) (T-D).

claims.text: Under section 168(k), the bonus depreciation allowance for qualified property placed in service in 2026 is 20 percent.
claims.real_world_why: 100 percent for property acquired after January 19, 2025; 20 percent applies only to property acquired before January 20, 2025 and placed in service in 2026.
claims.predicted_why: as B1; a year in words is not a date, so it is read as wording, not refused.

predictions: T-A (amends route, form-number match): each Public Law extract's printed amends line ('Section 164(b)(6) is amended', 'Section 6050W(e) is amended', 'Section 168(k)(2)(A) is amended') verifies and becomes an amends route; the code section's proposed form number ('§164', '§6050W', '§168', or none) is not a substring of that line, so the missing-document check reports the amended document absent though it is in the packet. Every claim that reaches decide ends unresolved (governing_instrument_absent). Cause: app/upload.py confirm (_core / containment, D10), built on ISO form numbers ('Form HO 00 03 Only'). Class (b).

T-R (rules rank lines, not documents): when the amends route is not recorded, rule 1 does not fire once the endorsement yields more than one confirmed line ('more than one in-scope endorsement'), and rule 2 ties among lines of the same document; amount claims end documents_disagree. Cause: arbiter._endorsement_over_base / _later_effective_date count assertions. Class (d).

T-D (the expected break, an amount as of a date): no claim about a year is answered right. A year in words is not read at all; a printed date is refused (B3). Lines for other years of the same schedule are confirmed with the line for the claim's year, and nothing selects among them. Class (a).
T-P (percentages): percentage claims are read as wording, never compared. Cause: grouping._AMOUNT_RE needs a currency mark, digit grouping or a scale word. Class (d).
T-V (claim vocabulary): 'IRC 6050W(e)' in a claim reads as a second amount ('IRC 6050', currency 'IRC'), refused more_than_one_value. Class (b).

T-K (kinds): a statute, an Act and an IRS notice have no kind of their own; they are confirmed as policy_form, endorsement and correspondence. The proposer leaves the kind blank or proposes one of these for at least one of the seven files. Class (b).
T-E (effective dates): for at least one Public Law extract the proposer quotes the first page's effective-date line, which belongs to another section, and the person corrects it. Class (c).
T-W: no claim comes back wrong against the real world (S2 and S4 are named risks).
T-0: no run exceeds $8 of live calls in total.
